items.english: At the next house they shut the door in great haste, and call and knock as they might, there was no answer. They tried three or four other houses, and were turned away at them all.
At their wits' end, Ryujiro and Kotora went back to the ferry landing where they had started. Night had already fallen, and the evening moon was out.

"All of this comes from my own carelessness. At this rate, even if I returned to Edo, even if my master is alive and well, I could not for shame show my face. I must change my plan. Come, Kotora, what say you. Go on ahead and give no thought to me."
notes: Ryujiro's sessha rendered as plain I to keep his samurai formality without archaism.

items.english: "How could I do such a thing?" Kotora's voice was in earnest.
"Forgive me, but I have a little money kept inside my belly band. Once we reach the town of Fukawa there will surely be a secondhand clothes shop. With the night to cover us, come, let us push on."
She took Ryujiro by the hand and made to walk along the edge of the channel.
"Wait a moment." It was a woman's voice from among the reeds. It was Living-Rope O-Tetsu.
"It was I who took your clothes. Your swords and everything else, I have hidden them all away."
O-Tetsu roughly tore Ryujiro and Kotora apart and stood between them, roaring at them.
Kotora started and began to tremble. Ryujiro, once he knew it was O-Tetsu, could not speak a word. He was like a gnat stared down by a toad.
notes: Simile kept literal as written; no softening of Ryujiro's passivity.

items.english: "I thought something of this sort would happen, so while you were getting yourself ready I sent my kobun running ahead along every road, to get our own people to spread a net in advance. And all the while I followed behind in disguise, and without ever knowing you were watched and followed, you fell in with this wench and walked the paths between the paddies as friendly as could be, all but tangled together. I was jealous enough even to envy the scarecrows that looked at you."
notes: Net and tangled kept literal to hold the binding web. The scarecrow clause is compressed in the Japanese; read as jealousy even of scarecrows that watched them.

data.say: Drafted the night refusal to O-Tetsu's reveal, keeping net and binding language literal.
